result.instructions: Tools for UpKeep, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Which work orders are overdue and who are they assigned to?"; "List the open high-priority work orders for the Boiler Room location."; "Which spare parts are below their minimum quantity?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes UpKeep data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run upkeep_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run upkeep_request_feature to record the request. Paid plan: Pro (unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month), $9/month or $90/year). Pro can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run upkeep_upgrade (plan "monthly" or "yearly"); it returns a payment link for the user to open. upkeep_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

assigned_by_user.description: Only records for this assigning user id.

request_id.description: UpKeep request id (a short string such as "HW2I379ErS").

tools.name: upkeep_create_request
tools.title: Create work request
tools.description: WRITE: submit a new work request for the maintenance team to approve (it appears in UpKeep's Requests list and may notify the approvers or the assignee). It is not a work order until approved. If the account has a request form configured, pass its field labels in `fields`. POST /requests.

category.description: Must be one of the account's configured categories.

fields.description: Request form values: each name must match a field label on the account's request form.

tools.name: upkeep_approve_request
tools.title: Approve work request
tools.description: WRITE: approve a pending work request, which converts it into a work order (it may notify the assignee). Needs a token whose role may approve requests. Approving a request that is already approved or declined fails with HTTP 409. POST /requests/{id}/approve.

request_id.description: UpKeep request id (a short string such as "HW2I379ErS").

tools.name: upkeep_create_work_order
tools.title: Create work order
tools.description: WRITE: create a new work order (it may notify the assignee and appears in UpKeep's work order board). Ids for asset, location and assignee come from the list tools. POST /work-orders.

category.description: Must be one of the account's configured work order categories.

tools.name: upkeep_update_work_order
tools.title: Update work order
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing work order: status (open, onHold, inProgress, complete), title, description, priority, due date or assignee. Only the fields you pass change; completing a work order may trigger the account's integrations (for example Zapier). Archiving and deleting are not offered. PATCH /work-orders/{id}.

work_order_id.description: UpKeep work order id (a short string such as "HW2I379ErS").

tools.name: upkeep_add_work_order_message
tools.title: Add work order message
tools.description: WRITE: post a message (comment) on a work order's activity thread; people following the work order may be notified. POST /work-orders/{id}/update-messages.

work_order_id.description: UpKeep work order id (a short string such as "HW2I379ErS").

tools.name: upkeep_update_part_quantity
tools.title: Update part quantity
tools.description: WRITE: set the quantity on hand (and optionally the minimum quantity that triggers a low-stock notification) of a part. This overwrites the stored number: read the part first and pass the new total, not the difference. PATCH /parts/{id}.

part_id.description: UpKeep part id (a short string such as "HW2I379ErS").

quantity.description: The new quantity on hand (a total).
